extracted.intended_audience: Media members, journalists, broadcasters, photographers, and online outlets seeking credentials or press information for the Washington Football Team
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and priorities the Washington Football Team uses to grant, deny, revoke, and manage media credentials and distribution of press information during the 2021 season. Covers who gets credentials, grounds for revocation, online eligibility, and procedural/contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media priority 1 — Broadcast partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcast partners, including television and radio personnel responsible for live broadcasts of Washington Football Team games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is listed as the highest priority when granting credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media priority 2 — Local beat reporters for large-scale local outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Local beat reporters who cover the team on a daily basis for large-scale local outlets, including newspapers, wire services, radio stations and television affiliates that cover Washington and the NFL on a regular basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High priority for credentials after broadcast partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media priority 3 — Large-scale national outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Large-scale national outlets, including national newspapers, magazines, television stations, websites and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National outlets are prioritized after local beat reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media priority 4 — Washington, D.C. metro area community publications and stations
rubrics_metrics.description: Washington, D.C. metro area community publications and stations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local metro community outlets are prioritized above out-of-town community outlets and blogs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media priority 5 — Out-of-town community outlets on specific assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Out-of-town community outlets on specific assignment to cover Washington personnel of unique interest to the outlet’s market (e.g.: a player’s hometown newspaper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritized when on specific assignment relevant to their market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media priority 6 — Blogs, internet radio and independent outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Blogs, internet radio and other independent outlets, whose merit and credential consideration is subject to the discretion of Washington Public Relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outlets receive lower priority and are evaluated at PR’s discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media priority 7 — Visiting scouts handled separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for visiting scouts are handled separately in accordance with the 2021 Scouting Policy as distributed to all NFL teams prior to the season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visiting scouts follow a distinct scouting policy, not this credential priority list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Season credential eligibility — consistent and substantial coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Season credentials will be reserved for organizations that provide consistent and substantial coverage of the Washington Football Team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Season credentials are limited and intended for outlets with ongoing substantive coverage; a season credential does not guarantee working space in media work areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Day-to-day credential issuance (non-seasonal)
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of seasonally credentialed Washington beat reporters who produce daily on-site reports, all credentials at both locations are approved and issued on a daily and/or game-by-game basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most credentials are granted per game/day rather than season-long, unless specified beat reporter status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass transferability and editorial-use requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Passes and credentials are transferable within the same media outlet for use by those serving an editorial function with proper notice and approval by Washington Public Relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers require proper notice/approval; passes used by any member of a credentialed outlet without specific editorial assignment or by non-working members are subject to revocation and will affect future credential decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-working use and revocation impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Passes used by non-working members of the organization or without specific editorial assignment are subject to revocation and will affect all future credentialing decisions by Washington Public Relations for that outlet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improper use has organization-level consequences for future credentialing, not just individual revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freelancer credential policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Credentials will not be issued to freelance writers or photographers without a specific assignment received in writing by the assigning organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of limited work space, freelancers must present written assignment confirmation from their assigning organization to be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online entity eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Credentials may be issued: a) to online entities that are affiliated with a national or regional media organization; or, b) to online entities that host a website that regularly and substantially reports on the National Football League or the Washington Football Team, and employs for that website at least one full-time permanent employee who writes a substantial majority of all material posted on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority for these sites will be based on potential audience at the discretion of Washington Public Relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for denial or revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Washington personnel may deny or revoke credentials without notice and an individual shall surrender his/her credential upon request for: noncompliance with the priorities or guidelines set out in this policy; noncompliance with health, safety, or security directives issued regarding Washington events; and for conduct for which there are reasonable grounds to believe violate state or federal law, or constitute a breach of professional ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial/revocation can be immediate and does not require prior notice; reasons include policy noncompliance, health/safety/security violations, and suspected illegal or unethical conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest process for denial or revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any organization that wishes to contest a denial or revocation may: a) request Washington Public Relations provide a written rationale for the denial or revocation; b) submit a written response to that rationale to the Washington Public Relations Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a two-step administrative process (request rationale, submit response) for appealing credential decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credential pickup/use affecting future requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If a credential is not picked up and/or used on game day, future credential requests may not be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to use an issued credential can negatively impact future credentialing for the outlet.

rubrics_metrics.name: COVID-19 protocols compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the duration of the 2021 season, the Washington Football Team will be abiding by the guidelines and protocols agreed upon by the NFL and NFLPA regarding the COVID-19 pandemic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credentialing and event access will be subject to NFL/NFLPA COVID-19 rules; noncompliance may be grounds for denial/revocation under health/safety directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media portal and media guide access
rubrics_metrics.description: Washington Football Team’s Public Relations department has a media website (https://washington.1rmg.com/) designed to serve the needs of all media members who cover the organization; the site contains the annual media guide and weekly game guides including stats, rosters, personnel bios and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary resource for media information; media can also access via Washingtonfootball.com under the Press Room tab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release distribution procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: All Washington Football Team press releases and weekly media packets are distributed via e-mail. Contact the Washington Public Relations department to be added to the team’s email distribution list for all press releases and media advisories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being on the email distribution list is the mechanism to receive official team press releases and media packets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy change reservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Washington Public Relations reserves the right to change this policy at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The team can modify credentialing policy unilaterally and at its discretion.
